$comment: Rule catalog — precision. Standard 12. Carries two prohibitions: excessive decimal precision, and calling a tiny modeled difference meaningful without justification.

rules.title: Stated precision does not exceed what the evidence supports
rules.description: The number of decimal places a probability is stated to is no finer than the standard error of an estimate from a sample that size.
rules.rationale: Writing 0.6237 from a sample of forty claims a resolution the data cannot deliver: the fourth decimal is noise presented as signal. Readers reasonably treat extra digits as extra information, and here they are the opposite.
rules.remediation: Round to the precision the sample supports, or state the probability with fewer digits in output.probabilityStated.
rules.$assuranceNote: The bound is the binomial standard error of a proportion, which is a heuristic: it assumes independent observations and takes the declared sample at face value. It catches obvious overstatement and will not catch precision inflated by correlated data.

rules.title: A tiny modeled difference is not called meaningful without justification
rules.description: Where a stated edge, or a departure from the baseline, falls below the project's materiality threshold, the record explains why it is nonetheless meaningful.
rules.rationale: A two-tenths-of-a-percent edge is well inside the error of almost any model that produced it, and acting on it is acting on noise. The threshold is a project judgement about its own models, which is why it lives in policy.
rules.remediation: Write edge.materialityNote explaining why the difference exceeds the model's own error, or stop presenting the difference as actionable.
rules.$assuranceNote: Compares a magnitude against a policy threshold and checks that an explanation exists. Whether the explanation is sound — whether the difference really does exceed the model's error — is not machine-checkable.
